key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize residential building energy management while making battery-control decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: For building energy systems with PV, storage, dynamic tariffs, and weather-dependent demand, the study shows that interpretable DRL can lower electricity costs and improve operational decision-making.
method: Trained on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for building energy control
Expanded the state space with demand, PV, battery state, electricity price, weather, calendar/holiday flags, and forecasts
Applied post-hoc explanation methods to interpret learned policies
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus (LLEC) data, with A2C and PPO outperforming off-policy methods in cumulative reward and policy stability.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality and completeness of forecasts and real-time measurements, and post-hoc explanations may not fully capture all policy behaviors.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
